GFL's special committee will take time to evaluate the bids and may ask the potential buyers to raise their offers, according to the report. No final decision has been made, and other bidders could emerge.
Energy Capital and Blackstone declined to comment to Bloomberg. Spokespeople for GFL, KKR, Brookfield, and IFM didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.
GFL CEO Patrick Dovigi told Bloomberg TV on Wednesday that he's open to taking the company private at a higher valuation than it currently trades at.

“We’re sort of in the third inning of a long baseball game,” Dovigi told the business news network, adding that no decision has been made by the company. “Obviously, we’re shareholders first and we like to explore all opportunities for all of our shareholders.”
